headline: 6 Naya Dhara leaders taken into custody after Press Club and DMCH clashes
summary: Police detained six party leaders following a clash with the Rashtra Sanglap Forum that disrupted emergency services at Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
details: Police took six leaders and activists of Naya Dhara Bangladesh into custody Tuesday night after a clash with the Rashtra Sanglap Forum near the Jatiya Press Club and a subsequent standoff at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).

The detainees include Naya Dhara Chairman Momin Mehedi, Senior Vice-Chairman Shanta Farzana, Vice-Chairman Dr Nurjahan Nira, and other senior officials. They were escorted from the hospital's emergency department under police protection around 11:10 pm.

The violence began Tuesday evening during a Naya Dhara program protesting an alleged assault on Shanta Farzana. Clashes broke out between Naya Dhara and the Rashtra Sanglap Forum, leaving several people injured on both sides.

The situation escalated at DMCH, where Rashtra Sanglap Forum members allegedly confined Naya Dhara leaders inside the emergency department for three hours, disrupting medical services for approximately 90 minutes.

Rashtra Sanglap Forum leaders claimed the clash started because Shanta Farzana made offensive remarks about July fighters and the BNP. Naya Dhara Chairman Momin Mehedi alleged that the Forum's member secretary attacked their program and stole journalists' phones.
Inspector Md Faruk of the DMCH police camp stated that the disorder created fear among patients and their attendants before police intervened to restore order.

headline_marked: Over 50 injured as [[Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash]] at Dhaka institutions
headline: Over 50 injured as Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash at Dhaka institutions
summary: Violent confrontations between student wings of BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami hit Alia Madrasa, Dhaka College, and JnU, leaving the principal of Alia Madrasa injured.
details: Clashes broke out between Chhatra Dal and Islami Chhatra Shibir activists across several educational institutions in Dhaka, including Dhaka Alia Madrasa, Dhaka College, and Jagannath University (JnU).

At Dhaka Alia Madrasa, the conflict centered on the occupation of the Allama Kashgari (R) Hall. After repeated clashes throughout Tuesday, Shibir activists reportedly left the hall, which was then occupied by Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal activists.
During the occupation of the hall, Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal activists allegedly carried out vandalism and assaulted the principal of Dhaka Alia Madrasa, Mohammad Obaidul Haque.

The violence at Alia Madrasa resulted in injuries to approximately 25 Shibir activists and over 30 Chhatra Dal members. Following the unrest, a Chhatra Dal leader locked the hall, citing security concerns for the students.
Similar violent encounters were reported at Dhaka College and Jagannath University, with both sides claiming scores of injuries in multiple rounds of fighting.
The unrest has turned several campus areas, including Bakshibazar, into battlegrounds as student wings continue to clash over institutional control.
